Based on my analysis of the repository, here are the files that implement file download functionality with the `Content-Disposition` header:

`lib/response.js`

`test/res.download.js`

`test/res.attachment.js`

`examples/downloads/index.js`

`test/acceptance/downloads.js`

These files implement the functionality through `res.download()` and `res.attachment()` methods which set the `Content-Disposition` header to `"attachment"` with an optional filename, causing browsers to save files instead of displaying them inline.

`lib/response.js`
`examples/downloads/index.js`

The `res.download()` method (and `res.attachment()`) set the `Content-Disposition` header to `attachment; filename="..."`, which instructs the browser to download and save the file with the chosen name instead of displaying it inline.

`lib/response.js`

The `res.attachment()` method (lines 604-612) and `res.download()` method (lines 433-482) both set the `Content-Disposition` header using the `content-disposition` package, which instructs the browser to save the file with a chosen name instead of displaying it inline.

`lib/response.js` - Core implementation of `res.download()` (line 433) and `res.attachment()` (line 604) methods that set the `Content-Disposition` header with the `attachment` directive.

`test/res.download.js` - Comprehensive tests demonstrating `res.download(path, filename)` usage to serve files with a chosen download name.

`test/res.attachment.js` - Tests for `res.attachment(filename)` method that sets the Content-Disposition header to enable file downloads.

`examples/downloads/index.js` - Practical example showing `res.download()` in action to handle file downloads with user-chosen filenames.

`test/acceptance/downloads.js` - Integration tests verifying the `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="..."` header is properly set.

**Why:** Handlers set the `Content-Disposition` HTTP response header to `attachment; filename="<chosen-name>"` to force browsers to download files instead of displaying them inline.

`lib/view.js`

This file implements the core template resolution logic: the constructor applies a default extension to the bare template name (lines 66-73), the `lookup()` method searches the root directories (lines 104-123), and the `resolve()` method tries to find the file either as `<path>.<ext>` or falls back to `<path>/index.<ext>` (lines 169-187).

`lib/view.js`

The `View.prototype.resolve` method implements the template resolution strategy: it first tries `<path>.<ext>`, and if that doesn't exist, it falls back to `<path>/index.<ext>`, with the extension coming from the default engine or explicit extension provided in the bare name.

`lib/view.js`

This file contains the core template resolution logic: the `View.prototype.resolve` method tries the file directly with the extension first (line 173-178), then falls back to checking for an `index` file inside a folder with the same name (line 181-186). The `tryStat` helper safely checks if each candidate file exists on disk.

`lib/view.js`

The `View.prototype.resolve` method (lines 169-187) implements the template lookup by first trying to resolve `<path>.<ext>`, and if that file doesn't exist, falling back to `<path>/index.<ext>` to look for an index file in a folder, while the constructor and `lookup` method handle applying the default extension when no extension is provided.
